audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] gives Trundle Levels 1 through 6 outright, while whys[1] to whys[5] in the same object say Aatrox trades back at 2, answers his brawl at 3, drains ahead at 4-5, out-drains him at 6 whenever Subjugate is down, and out-values him at first item. The packet chart for this matchup reads Skill at Level 1 and Aatrox at every stage after.
audit.why: The mirror at audits/top/trundle__aatrox.json keeps an early-bully framing for Trundle, so I have NOT flipped the chart — the two directions must not contradict. But the entry disagrees with itself, and the packet has Aatrox at 57.4% over 763 games, the highest win rate in this slice.
audit.corrected: No edit proposed. Raised for the user in questionsForUser — the mirror and the packet point opposite ways and one of them has to move.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice, Chomp and Subjugate are named repeatedly with no cooldowns, so 'the moment they're down' has nothing to count.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice is 21/19.5/18/16.5/15, Chomp is a flat 3.5s, Frozen Domain 18/17/16/15/14, Subjugate 120/100/80. The 3.5s Chomp is the important one — the entry tells you to wait for Bite to be down, but it is never down for long; the real window is Pillar.
audit.corrected: 21s Pillar, 3.5s Chomp and 120s Subjugate written into spikes[0], spikes[1] and mid, and the trade window re-anchored onto Pillar rather than Chomp.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice is described as a slow that 'splits your combo'. It is impassable terrain. Dropped on top of you it physically blocks Umbral Dash, which is the single reason this lane is hard — and the entry never says it. Frozen Domain also increases the healing he receives from ALL sources while he stands on it, which is what makes his drain war winnable.
audit.why: Riot's text: Pillar of Ice — 'Trundle creates an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain and slowing all nearby enemy units'; Frozen Domain — 'gaining Attack Speed, Move Speed, and increased healing from all sources while on it'; King's Tribute — 'When an enemy unit dies near Trundle, he heals for a percent of its maximum Health.' So he sustains off the wave for free, amplifies it on his zone, and walls off your only mobility tool. The mirror reaches the same conclusion from the other side.
audit.corrected: Pillar named as impassable terrain that blocks Umbral Dash (9s at rank 1); Frozen Domain's healing amplification and King's Tribute's wave sustain stated as the reason to bring Grievous Wounds.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole entry is a drain war and never names anti-heal, and it never says that stacking resistances is the wrong response to Subjugate.
audit.why: Subjugate steals a percentage of your Health, Armor and Magic Resistance and doubles the amount stolen over four seconds — so every point of armour you buy is a point he can take. King's Tribute and Frozen Domain make Grievous Wounds the item that decides the extended fight.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal stated in spikes[2]; the resistance-stealing of Subjugate stated in the full-layer tldr.

edits.before: Your window: play around his Pillar of Ice and Bite, and the moment they're down land Q3 sweetspot into W fast and drain — with those cooldowns spent his short-range brawl can't answer your combo.
edits.after: Your window is Pillar of Ice (21s), not Chomp — Chomp is back every 3.5s. Pillar is impassable terrain, so dropped on you it walls off Umbral Dash entirely. Fight only once it is spent, then Q3 into chains fast.

edits.before: Trundle R Subjugate steals resistances and heals off you, so don't extend blindly into his ult — but your World Ender heal-amp still out-drains him when his R is on cooldown, so time your all-in around it.
edits.after: Subjugate (120s) steals your Health, Armor and MR outright, and doubles the theft over 4s — so never extend into it. Your World Ender heal amp out-drains him whenever that 120s is down; both ults are on the same clock.

edits.before: Your bruiser spike and full Q pattern tip the drain war your way; keep hitting on his Pillar/Bite windows and your sustain out-values his.
edits.after: Your bruiser spike tips the drain war your way, but buy Grievous Wounds — King's Tribute heals him off each dying minion, and Frozen Domain amps it.

edits.before: From level 2-3 the lane tips to you. Trundle still dictates tempo with Pillar of Ice — it slows you out of Q sweetspot range and splits your combo — but play around it: the moment his Pillar and Bite are both down, land Q3 into W Infernal Chains fast and drain before he can re-zone you. Level 6 adds R Subjugate, which steals your resistances and heals off you, so don't extend into his ult; time your all-ins for when it's down and your heal amp out-drains him.
edits.after: From level 2-3 the lane tips to you. Pillar of Ice is not a slow, it is impassable terrain — dropped under you it blocks Umbral Dash outright, and that 21s is the only cooldown worth tracking, since Chomp returns every 3.5s. Once Pillar is spent, land Q3 into Infernal Chains fast and drain before he can re-zone you. At 6 Subjugate steals your Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft over 4s, so all-in only on that 120s.

edits.before: Split your combo with Pillar of Ice + slow
edits.after: Wall off Umbral Dash with Pillar of Ice

edits.before: Trundle changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Trundle pillar, W zone, and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Trundle wants to force long trades, punish overextension, and turn one bad Aatrox cooldown into a lane-losing fight.
edits.after: Trundle changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Pillar of Ice (E, 21s), impassable terrain that walls off Umbral Dash, and a Subjugate that steals his Health, Armor and MR. Aatrox wins by fighting in the window Pillar is spent, spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, and buying Grievous Wounds — armour alone is exactly what Trundle takes off him.

edits.before: Trundle pillar, W zone, and R

notes: Level chart NOT changed, deliberately. The mirror audits/top/trundle__aatrox.json preserves an early-bully framing for Trundle, and the content win[] here agrees with it, but the entry's own whys[1..5] and the packet chart both hand Aatrox everything from Level 2. Changing one side would put the two directions into direct contradiction, so this is raised as a question rather than guessed. The mirror also records that packets/trundle.json gives 49.21% while MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.aatrox gives 42.6 — one of those is stale, and Aatrox's own packet says 57.4%.
